reason: The plant needs separate receivers to collect the gases from water, so I’ll start by fitting the hydrogen receiver.
expectation: I expect the hydrogen receiver to connect to the electrolysis unit; I’m unsure whether collection will start before the oxygen receiver is fitted.

Capturing carbon dioxide is also a goal, but I’ll begin with the two receivers at the electrolysis unit.

effect: The hydrogen receiver collects gas immediately, while oxygen follows a separate circuit. I’ll fit the oxygen receiver to complete the water-splitting collection.
reaction: I was surprised collection started with only the hydrogen receiver fitted.
reason: The oxygen receiver belongs on the electrolysis unit and should collect the other gas needed for the goal.
expectation: I expect it to connect to the separate oxygen circuit and collect oxygen, completing the water electrolysis goal.

alternatives.reason: Carbon dioxide capture is also required, but I want to finish fitting the electrolysis receivers first.

effect: The oxygen receiver completed the water-splitting goal, and I now know the oxygen is intended as oxidizer for the lander.
reaction: The distinction between oxygen as oxidizer and hydrogen as fuel made the plant’s purpose clearer.
reason: Carbon dioxide capture is the remaining goal, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the receiver to connect to the capture unit and collect compressed carbon dioxide, though I’m unsure whether another step will be needed.

effect: The capture unit completed the remaining goal by separating carbon dioxide from Martian air and storing it under pressure. The plant has gathered its ingredients, though I have not seen how they are used next.
reaction: Gathering an ingredient from the thin air was satisfying, though I was curious what the plant would do with it.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the oxygen receiver was most worthwhile because the explanation clarified oxygen’s role as the lander’s oxidizer and distinguished it from fuel.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the hydrogen receiver was straightforward, with little decision-making beyond choosing which receiver to install first.

surprise.text: I was surprised that hydrogen collection started before the oxygen receiver was fitted.

arbitrary.text: The order of fitting the two electrolysis receivers felt somewhat arbitrary; both were clearly needed, but neither seemed to demand being first.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to learn how the collected gases support the early ascent and what the distant core reveals.
